trial.title: A Brief Intervention for Cannabis Use

endpoints.description: The TLFB is a calendar based assessment that is able to capture the frequency and quantity of substance use and other measurable behaviors. Responders identify anchor dates to facilitate recall of days in which substances were used.

This is a 23-item assessment of the frequency in which problems or negative consequences associated with cannabis use have occurred. For each item, participants select 0 times, 1-2 times, 3-5 times, 6-10 times, or 10+ times in the past month. Higher scores on this inventory indicate a higher frequency of problems or consequences experienced.

endpoints.measure: Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview (MINI) Cannabis Use Disorder Module
endpoints.description: This is a 12-item semi-structured clinician interview that assesses diagnostic symptom criteria of cannabis use disorder (CUD) from the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual 5th Edition (DSM-5). Clinicians select either 'yes' or 'no' for the presence of the symptom.

This is a relatively brief objective assessment of recent cannabis use that is collected through mouth swab and is tested at Forensic Fluids Laboratory for the presence of delta-9 tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), delta-8 THC, and cannabidiol (CBD) using a cut-off of 1 nanogram/liter.

analysis_trace: Trial NCT06395389 is a pilot randomized trial comparing Bloom (values-based brief intervention) vs Health Education for emerging adults (18-25) with frequent cannabis use. Sample size n=62 estimated. Primary endpoint TLFB measures cannabis use frequency/quantity. Secondary endpoints include MAPI (problems), MINI (CUD diagnosis), and oral fluid THC. Evidence from motivational interviewing meta-analyses (Calomarde-Gomez et al.) shows MI reduces cannabis use and achieves abstinence in adults. Brief interventions for cannabis in emerging adults show modest effect sizes (g≈0.2-0.4) for use reduction. As a pilot trial, primary goal is feasibility and preliminary efficacy signals. Bloom's values-based approach aligns with MI principles suggesting potential superiority over health education. Expected TLFB reduction: Bloom 20-30% greater than Health Education. Expected MAPI reduction: small-to-moderate favoring Bloom. MINI CUD remission: modest rates favoring Bloom. Oral fluid: biochemical verification expected to correlate with self-report.
